items.title: Steve O'Neill, County Councillor Ward 4 provided an update including
notes: recent approval by the County of a 4.6% tax increase for 2024, an increase to the cost of the County yellow garbage bags effective July 1, 2024, province wide changes to blue box collection, upcoming health and housing symposium on January 30th to address housing and homelessness, changes to the composition of the County Social Services Committee, and the release of the tender for an automated speed enforcement program.

County Councillor O’Neill responded to questions regarding increasing the locations to purchase yellow garbage bags, the housing and homelessness symposium and lack of social services resources in the rural areas.

notes: Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. However, any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate discussion and/or action.
THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves consent agenda items 10.1 through 10.6 as follows:

items.title: 2024 Community Impact Grant Recommendations
notes: Report from K. Drexler, Manager of Community Development Mayor Watters declared a conflict of pecuniary interest with respect to the 2024 Community Impact Grants as Riverfest has an office located at the Elora Centre for the Arts.
Mayor Watters, having declared a conflict of interest, left the meeting and Deputy Mayor Wilton assumed the Chair.

K. Drexler, Manager of Community Development provided an overview of the report, including the review and scoring process for the various applications. She responded to questions regarding future review of the policy, concerns raised at the advisory committee and the Canada Food Day application.

items.title: Strategic Plan Review - 2024

K. Martin, Manager of Strategic Initiatives and Communications provided a brief overview of the report.
Mayor Watters called for a 3 minute recess.

items.title: Declaration of Surplus Lands
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services provided an overview of the report, indicating the Wellington Catholic District School Board (WCDSB) is wishing to expand St. Joseph Catholic School and perhaps include a future high school. The Township can assist the WCDSB by selling Strathallan Park to the Board for the purpose of expanding the school.
Members of Council expressed concerns with the loss of green space in the area, the impact on property values, and traffic implications.
In response to a question, the Municipal Solicitor noted the sale is subject to Ministry approval and a public planning process where more detail will be provided on the development of the site.
8.4 John Mascarin re: Conflict of Interest Training
John Mascarin, Integrity Commissioner delivered training for Members of Council on the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act and responded to questions.
Mayor Watters called for a 5 minute recess.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington pass a by-law to stop up and close Francis Lane, Registered Plan 181, Elora for the purpose of conveying the road allowance to the abutting landowner, Kat Florence Canada Company Limited; AND THAT the Council direct the Managing Director of Infrastructure Services to provide public notice of the Township’s intent to sell Francis Lane at the subject property and on the Township’s website for notice period of 10 business days; AND THAT the Council authorize the Mayor and Clerk to execute an Agreement of Purchase and Sale, as amended, between The Corporation of the Township of Centre Wellington and Kat Florence Canada Company Limited for the purchase of Township-owned lands known as Francis Lane in Elora for the purpose of a pedestrian walkway in the amount of $160,000; AND THAT the Chief Administrative Officer be delegated authority to execute all ancillary documents in relation thereto to cause the Lands to be conveyed to the purchaser.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington direct staff to investigate and work towards supporting the development of a child-care facility/recreational space to be located in Belwood. This includes the collaboration and coordination between other levels of government and community partners; AND THAT the investigation include the high level identification of a site, planning issues, financial implications and facility management. A public process including input from the Belwood Community Development Committee would also form part of this planning process; AND THAT staff be instructed to bring back a report to Council, including letters of intent from community partners and other levels of government, at the June 24th meeting, providing background information and details to facilitate the next phase of this potential development.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion from Councillor Wilton – Transportation Master Plan
motions.text: WHEREAS the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington recognizes the urgent need for a transportation bypass around Fergus; The Council of the Township of Centre Wellington resolves that the second by-pass option identified in the Township’s 2019 Transportation Master Plan (p. 74) that would see a new bridge constructed at County Road 29 and crossing to land that is immediately adjacent to the Pierpoint Fly Fishing Nature Reserve is no longer a viable option; AND THAT Council directs staff to refer to this resolution in future transportation planning discussions with Wellington County and the Ministry of Transportation of Ontario; AND THAT this resolution be circulated to the staff and Council of Wellington County.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion from Councillor Wilton – Transportation Master Plan
motions.text: WHEREAS, all Ontarians deserve and expect a safe and respectful workplace; AND WHEREAS, municipal governments, as the democratic institutions most directly engaged with Ontarians need respectful discourse; AND WHEREAS, several incidents in recent years of disrespectful behaviour and workplace harassment have occurred amongst members of municipal councils; AND WHEREAS, these incidents seriously and negatively affect the people involved and lower public perceptions of local governments; AND WHEREAS, Municipal Codes of Conduct are helpful tools to set expectations of council member behaviour; AND WHEREAS, municipal governments do not have the necessary tools to adequately enforce compliance with municipal Codes of Conduct; AND WHEREAS 201 municipalities support the call for legislation to ensure appropriate accountability measures for sitting councillors, including OBCM, AMO and ROMA; AND WHEREAS a fundamental, underlying principle of broadening diversity, equity and inclusion in politics rests on the assumption that the workplace is safe; AND WHEREAS we believe that municipal elected officials should be held to account in this way, we also believe that federal and provincial elected officials should take similar actions to hold themselves to account; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: The Council of the Township of Centre Wellington supports the call of the Association of Municipalities of Ontario for the Government of Ontario to introduce legislation to strengthen Municipal Codes of Conduct and compliance with them in consultation with municipal governments; AND THAT legislation encompass the Association of Municipalities of Ontario’s recommendations for: a. Updating Municipal Codes of Conduct to account for workplace safety and harassment, b. Creating a flexible administrative penalty regime, adapted to the local economic, c. Increasing training of municipal Integrity Commissioners to enhance consistency of investigations and recommendations across the province, d. Allowing municipalities to apply to a member of the judiciary to remove a sitting member if recommended through the report of a Municipal Integrity Commissioner, e. Prohibit a member so removed from sitting for election in the term of removal and the subsequent term of office. AND THAT this motion be circulated to the Right Honourable Justin Trudeau, Prime Minister of Canada, the Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, the Honourable David Lametti the Minister of Justice, the Honourable Paul Calandra, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Kate Manson-Smith, Deputy Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Scott Pierce, Federation of Canadian Municipalities Acting President, and Colin Best, President of the Association of Municipalities of Ontario.
